source_text: Important geological concepts were established as naturalists began studying the rock formations of the Alps in the 18th century. question: What percentage of a bar-tailed godwit's bodyweight is stored as fat to fuel its migration journey?
explanation: Some bar-tailed godwits have a remarkable ability to store fat to fuel their migrations, allowing them to fly long distances without stopping for food.
source_text: Some bar-tailed godwits Limosa lapponica have the longest known non-stop flight of any migrant, flying 11,000 km from Alaska to their New Zealand non-breeding areas. Prior to migration, 55 percent of their bodyweight is stored as fat to fuel this uninterrupted journey.
